title: strpos False vs Zero Comparison Hazard
platform_conditions: PHP 7.4/8.x; preg_match returns false instead of 0 when pcre.backtracking_limit (default 1,000,000) is exceeded
security_mechanism: strpos() returns the match offset — 0 for a prefix match — and false when there is none; because 0 == false under loose comparison, if (strpos($url, $prefix) == false) treats the exactly-matching attacker-chosen input as a failure while accepting everything else, inverting the check. Similar quirks compose into fail-open gates: @ suppresses the error from a failed call so execution continues on an invalid value, intval()/(int) stop at the first non-digit ('123abc' becomes 123), and is_numeric accepts exponential notation ('1e3'). preg_match returns false — not 0 — when the backtrack limit is hit, so an adversarial subject makes a validator's return indistinguishable from 'no match' unless the caller compares === 1, and a pattern ending in $ still matches before a trailing newline because $ anchors to the end-or-before-final-newline position.

source_sink_clues.source: Any attacker-controlled scalar flowing into these idioms: URLs validated by strpos prefixes, filter inputs validated by preg_match, numeric strings passed through (int)/is_numeric.
source_sink_clues.sink: Loose == / != tests of strpos results on security gates; @-suppressed calls whose results feed checks; (int)/intval coercion before authorization decisions; preg_match validators not compared with === 1

tracking_guards: Require !== false / !== 0 three-way comparisons with explicit handling of both outcomes; require that no @ operator sits on a security-relevant call and that null/false results are handled; require preg_match(...) === 1 with \A...\z anchors and explicit newline rejection; require strict type validation before numeric coercion.
not_candidate_when: Return values are tested with !== and both the false and 0 cases are handled explicitly with the intended meaning, @ is confined to non-security cleanup whose results are validated afterwards, or the validator anchors with \A/\z, rejects trailing newlines, and compares preg_match results with === 1.
